William Shakespeare, A Midsummer Night’s Dream.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/william-shakespeare/a-midsummer-nights-dream

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- William Shakespeare, the author, died 1616.

First publication of the text used: A Midsummer Night’s Dream was published in 1600 by William Shakespeare.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1600, before 1931. Standard Ebooks states that the text is in the United States public domain (quoted below). A work published in 1600 enters the United States public domain on 1 January 1696.
- Country of origin: every person whose words are in the text died in 1925 or earlier (the last died in 1616), so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: A Midsummer Night’s Dream was published in 1600 by William Shakespeare.
- Wikidata Q692 (William Shakespeare), P570 = 1616-04-23; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare
